Higher body mass index (BMI) has been found to be associated with poor asthma control in urban populations. This is because excess weight can lead to increased inflammation, airway obstruction, and decreased lung function, all of which can make it more challenging to manage asthma symptoms.

In the context of this question, four validated asthma control questionnaires were used to assess the relationship between BMI and asthma control. While no association was found between obesity and asthma control in an urban population with asthma, weight loss may not be an effective strategy for improving asthma control in this group.

This suggests that simply losing weight may not lead to significant improvements in asthma symptoms or quality of life for individuals who already have asthma. However, it's essential to note that addressing the root causes of excess weight and adopting a healthy lifestyle can still help manage asthma symptoms and improve overall well-being.

It's also worth mentioning that the relationship between BMI and asthma control may be influenced by other factors, such as socioeconomic status, access to healthcare, and cultural attitudes towards body image. Therefore, a more comprehensive approach that takes these factors into account is likely to be more effective in improving asthma outcomes.

In summary, while there was no association found between higher BMI and worse asthma control in an urban population with asthma, addressing excess weight through lifestyle modifications may still be beneficial for individuals who experience persistent or severe asthma symptoms.
